I farm wheat and maize on the same 24 mu, so this year I will keep the full wheat-maize rotation on all 24 mu. I am 70 and there are only 2 people in my household, so I will keep things steady and simple instead of taking risks. I have grown these crops for many years, and with well irrigation I will rely on the usual local way: stable improved seed for wheat, hybrid seed for maize, moderate fertilizer, enough irrigation for key stages, and not too many pesticide sprays. I will use rotary tillage because it saves labor compared with deep ploughing and still works well on my land. For wheat, I will push yield with a little more water and fertilizer because it responds well under irrigation. For maize, I will also plant the full 24 mu after wheat harvest and manage it for a solid yield, but I will not overuse inputs because I want dependable returns and less labor pressure.
